problem_text:
A city planner must distribute a fixed budget across 18 neighborhood improvement projects to maximize total community benefit.  
Each project has the following characteristics:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.128, impact factor 0.115, allocation range [0.022, 0.799]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.135, impact factor 0.069, allocation range [0.075, 0.550]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.045, impact factor 0.257, allocation range [0.012, 0.759]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.190, impact factor 0.115, allocation range [0.070, 0.582]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.186, impact factor 0.147, allocation range [0.014, 0.384]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.089, impact factor 0.049, allocation range [0.073, 0.616]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.119, impact factor 0.042, allocation range [0.070, 0.869]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.117, impact factor 0.274, allocation range [0.042, 0.582]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.109, impact factor 0.115, allocation range [0.005, 0.734]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.117, impact factor 0.256, allocation range [0.011, 0.566]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.061, impact factor 0.236, allocation range [0.058, 0.687]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.035, impact factor 0.050, allocation range [0.048, 0.308]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.149, impact factor 0.144, allocation range [0.059, 0.367]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.115, impact factor 0.252, allocation range [0.016, 0.336]  
* Project O: benefit score 0.160, impact factor 0.170, allocation range [0.015, 0.685]  
* Project P: benefit score 0.166, impact factor 0.280, allocation range [0.014, 0.663]  
* Project Q: benefit score 0.059, impact factor 0.132, allocation range [0.025, 0.404]  
* Project R: benefit score 0.036, impact factor 0.071, allocation range [0.001, 0.396]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified allocation range, and all shares must sum to the total budget. To ensure rapid implementation, the set of quick-start projects QS = {K, O, P} must collectively receive at least 0.149 of the total budget. Additionally, the overall implementation complexity, measured by a composite index, must not exceed 0.174, and the total community benefit must be at least 0.087. Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes total community benefit while satisfying all constraints.
